\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Estimate \AtlasInlineMath{\tau=\operatorname{tr}(A)}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
Assume \AtlasInlineMath{A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0} and \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}}; the zero matrix is allowed.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The data \AtlasInlineMath{d,\varepsilon,\delta} are public and \AtlasInlineMath{A} is hidden. Any query \AtlasInlineMath{v\in\mathbb{R}^d} returns exact \AtlasInlineMath{Av}. Responses have no sampling noise; randomized probes arise from the algorithm’s private randomness.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return any real \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat\tau}, without an additional confidence interval or certificate.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The success event is \AtlasInlineMath{|\widehat\tau-\tau|\le\varepsilon\tau}. For \AtlasInlineMath{\tau>0} this corresponds to relative loss \AtlasInlineMath{|\widehat\tau-\tau|/\tau}; when \AtlasInlineMath{\tau=0}, require \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat\tau=0}. Positive semidefiniteness ensures \AtlasInlineMath{\tau\ge0}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Count right products with single vectors only: \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized adaptive}
Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least \AtlasInlineMath{1-\delta}.

\textbf{Budget convention.} A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized nonadaptive}
Randomization is allowed, but all query vectors must be chosen at once from public inputs and the private seed. Responses may be used only for final postprocessing and cannot alter the queries. No further span, internal-computation, storage, or communication restriction is imposed; parallel organization does not change per-column charging.

The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least \AtlasInlineMath{1-\delta}.

\textbf{Budget convention.} A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

\textbf{Region.} \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge1}, \AtlasInlineMath{0<\varepsilon<1}, \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta<1/2}.

\textbf{Gap or comparison.} \AtlasInlineMath{O(\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)}+\varepsilon\log(1/\delta))}, and therefore \AtlasInlineMath{O(\log(1/\delta))}; the dimension cap can reduce this ratio.

\textbf{Comparison argument.} The independent local proof MX\_\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}TRACE\_\allowbreak{}PSD\_\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}proof\_\allowbreak{}uniform\_\allowbreak{}confidence\_\allowbreak{}wishart converts the adaptive Wishart posterior into a success-probability lower bound. Its small-tolerance success ceiling is 5/12<1/2, so the lower bound applies to every 0<delta<1/2; zero-query indistinguishability covers small dimensions and larger nontrivial tolerances. This does not use a finite-bit lower bound or substitute mean-square error for probability. Retain the minimum of Hutch++ and deterministic reconstruction for the upper side. Writing L=log(1/delta), the envelope ratio is O(min\{d,sqrt(L)/epsilon+L\}/min\{d,1/epsilon\}), bounded by O(sqrt(L)+epsilon L), hence O(L). No sharp confidence-dependent lower rate is asserted.

\textbf{Derivation.} \textbf{Claim and scope.} For every integer \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge1} and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\varepsilon<1}, any randomized adaptive exact matrix-vector algorithm with a fixed worst-case budget that guarantees

\AtlasMath{\Pr\bigl(|\widehat\tau-\operatorname{tr}(A)|\le\varepsilon\operatorname{tr}(A)\bigr)\ge2/3}

for every real positive semidefinite matrix of order \AtlasInlineMath{d} requires \AtlasInlineMath{\Omega(\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\})} queries. Queries may be arbitrary real vectors and the output any measurable function of the transcript. This argument concerns constant success probability; it does not establish sharp dependence on arbitrary confidence levels.

\textbf{Posterior lemma.} Use Lemma 13 of Braverman, Hazan, Simchowitz, and Woodworth (2020), or the unnormalized formulation in Proposition 3 and Appendix B.1 of *Fixed-Sparsity Matrix Approximation* (arXiv:2402.09379v3). Let \AtlasInlineMath{W=G^{\mathsf T}G}, where \AtlasInlineMath{G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}} has independent standard Gaussian entries. After at most \AtlasInlineMath{q<n} adaptive queries, include the private seed in the transcript \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal H}. A transcript-measurable orthogonal basis expresses the conditional matrix as a known matrix plus the Gram matrix of an independent standard Gaussian block of size \AtlasInlineMath{(n-q)\times(n-q)}. Thus

\AtlasMath{\operatorname{tr}(W)\mid\mathcal H=c(\mathcal H)+Z,\qquad Z\sim\chi^2_{(n-q)^2},}

where \AtlasInlineMath{Z} is independent of the transcript. Remove the component in the previously queried subspace from a dependent query. If the algorithm stops early, extend the transcript to \AtlasInlineMath{q} independent directions; its output remains measurable with respect to the extended transcript. This only provides additional information. For randomized algorithms, condition first on the independent private seed, apply the lemma, and then integrate. Adaptivity is preserved throughout.

For \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge4}, set \AtlasInlineMath{n=\min\{d,\lfloor1/(96\varepsilon)\rfloor\}}, so \AtlasInlineMath{n\ge4}, and let \AtlasInlineMath{A=\operatorname{diag}(W,0_{d-n})}. A query in dimension \AtlasInlineMath{d} returns the \AtlasInlineMath{W} product of its first \AtlasInlineMath{n} coordinates and a zero tail, exactly simulating one query in dimension \AtlasInlineMath{n}. The matrix \AtlasInlineMath{A} is positive semidefinite and \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(A)=n^2}.

\textbf{Anti-concentration.} Suppose \AtlasInlineMath{q\le n/2}. For \AtlasInlineMath{Z\sim\chi^2_\nu} with \AtlasInlineMath{\nu\ge4}, the density is bounded by \AtlasInlineMath{1/\sqrt\nu}. Its maximum occurs at \AtlasInlineMath{\nu-2}; the standard Stirling lower bound for the Gamma function, with \AtlasInlineMath{a=\nu/2\ge2}, gives the bound \AtlasInlineMath{e(1-1/a)^{a-1}/(2\sqrt{2\pi a})\le1/\sqrt{2a}}. Here \AtlasInlineMath{\nu=(n-q)^2}, so the conditional trace density is at most \AtlasInlineMath{2/n}. Markov's inequality gives \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr(\operatorname{tr}(A)>4n^2)\le1/4}. On success and \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{tr}(A)\le4n^2}, the true trace lies in an interval of length \AtlasInlineMath{8\varepsilon n^2} centered at the transcript-measurable estimate \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat\tau}. Integrating the conditional density yields

\AtlasMath{\Pr(\text{success})\le\frac14+(8\varepsilon n^2)\frac2n=\frac14+16\varepsilon n\le\frac5{12}<\frac23.}

This contradicts success probability at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3} on every fixed input, which would imply average success at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3} under this admissible input distribution. Consequently the budget exceeds \AtlasInlineMath{n/2}, and \AtlasInlineMath{n} is a universal constant multiple of \AtlasInlineMath{\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\}}.

\textbf{Small dimensions.} For \AtlasInlineMath{d<4}, the output distribution of a zero-query algorithm is independent of the matrix. The permitted relative-error intervals for \AtlasInlineMath{I_d} and \AtlasInlineMath{2I_d} are disjoint when \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon\le1/384}. Both success probabilities therefore cannot be at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3}. One necessary query gives the required constant-factor lower bound.

\textbf{Remaining nontrivial tolerances.} Let \AtlasInlineMath{1/384<\varepsilon<1} and take any \AtlasInlineMath{d\ge1}. Choose \AtlasInlineMath{a_0>(1+\varepsilon)/(1-\varepsilon)}. The acceptable output intervals for \AtlasInlineMath{I_d} and \AtlasInlineMath{a_0I_d} are

\AtlasMath{[(1-\varepsilon)d,(1+\varepsilon)d],\qquad [(1-\varepsilon)a_0d,(1+\varepsilon)a_0d],}

and are disjoint. A zero-query algorithm has the same output distribution on both inputs, so its two success probabilities sum to at most \AtlasInlineMath{1} and cannot both be at least \AtlasInlineMath{2/3}. The fixed budget is therefore at least \AtlasInlineMath{1}. Since \AtlasInlineMath{\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\}\le384},

\AtlasMath{N\ge1\ge\frac1{384}\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\}.}

Combining the constants gives the uniform lower bound \AtlasInlineMath{\Omega(\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\})} for all \AtlasInlineMath{0<\varepsilon<1}. The scales of these inputs are neither revealed nor bounded, as required by the stated trace-estimation models.

The lower bound also applies at success probability \AtlasInlineMath{0.9}, uniformly for \AtlasInlineMath{b_{\mathrm q}\ge0}. Together with the admissible Rademacher NA-Hutch++ upper bound and reconstruction in \AtlasInlineMath{d} standard-basis queries, this yields \AtlasInlineMath{\Theta(\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\})}. This is an explicit consequence of the cited posterior lemma, rather than a trace-estimation theorem attributed directly to that source.

\AtlasMath{|\widehat\tau-\operatorname{tr}(A)|=\operatorname{tr}(A)\le\varepsilon\operatorname{tr}(A).}

for every input. It works at every allowed confidence level, dimension, and integer query alphabet. Nonnegativity of query cost makes the optimum exactly \AtlasInlineMath{0}. \textbf{Guarantee conversion.} The hard-distribution average success ceiling is 5/12 for the small-tolerance branch. Every target guarantee has success at least 1-delta>1/2, yielding a contradiction. Conditioning on the independent private seed covers randomized adaptive algorithms.

\textbf{Output rule.} Any real transcript-measurable trace estimate is allowed.

\textbf{Resource conversion.} N is the fixed worst-case number of right single-vector products for every input and private seed. A block costs its number of columns; internal arithmetic and postprocessing remain free.

\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{N.}

\AtlasMath{N\ge(1/384)\min\{d,1/\varepsilon\}}
\textbf{Constants.} The displayed constant 1/384 is universal and independent of d, epsilon, and delta.

\textbf{Local argument.} MX\_\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}TRACE\_\allowbreak{}PSD\_\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}proof\_\allowbreak{}uniform\_\allowbreak{}confidence\_\allowbreak{}wishart

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.09379v3}{[2]} pdf pages: 11; 22; 23; section: Section 3.1; Appendix B.1; theorem: Proposition 3; proof in Appendix B.1

Primary version: arXiv:2402.09379v3, revision dated 2024-03-26. Archived source SHA256 efb3338e536779388499ff92beee30a07154993989b2a743138f51d620d246c1. Decisive source\_\allowbreak{}read ranges: [26800,31000) and [51800,59600).

The square specialization gives a transcript-measurable known matrix plus an independent (n-q)-by-(n-q) Gaussian Gram block after q adaptive directions. Known deterministic scaling accommodates normalized Gaussian conventions.

The source sparsity-approximation theorem is not asserted as a trace-estimation lower bound; the separate local proof supplies the probability bound, dimension embedding, private-seed conditioning, and endpoint cases.

Native pointer: /proofs/1/body; canonical SHA-256: 829031cb74a102ed98948ae4234f2ae0d111a259b503a585d197b1cbe11d9224

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy **Claim and scope.** For every integer \$d\textbackslash{}ge1\$ and \$0<\textbackslash{}varepsilon<1\$,\allowbreak{} any randomized adaptive exact matrix-vector algorithm with a fixed worst-case budget that guarantees\newline{}\$\$\textbackslash{}Pr\textbackslash{}bigl(|\textbackslash{}widehat\textbackslash{}tau-\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)|\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)\textbackslash{}bigr)\textbackslash{}ge2/\allowbreak{}3\$\$\newline{}for every real positive semidefinite matrix of order \$d\$ requires \$\textbackslash{}Omega(\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\})\$ queries. Queries may be arbitrary real vectors and the output any measurable function of the transcript. This argument concerns constant success probability;\allowbreak{} it does not establish sharp dependence on arbitrary confidence levels.\newline{}\newline{}**Posterior lemma.** Use Lemma 13 of Braverman,\allowbreak{} Hazan,\allowbreak{} Simchowitz,\allowbreak{} and Woodworth (2020),\allowbreak{} or the unnormalized formulation in Proposition 3 and Appendix B.1 of *Fixed-Sparsity Matrix Approximation* (arXiv:\allowbreak{}2402.09379v3). Let \$W=\allowbreak{}G\textasciicircum{}\{\textbackslash{}mathsf T\}G\$,\allowbreak{} where \$G\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}mathbb R\textasciicircum{}\{n\textbackslash{}times n\}\$ has independent standard Gaussian entries. After at most \$q<n\$ adaptive queries,\allowbreak{} include the private seed in the transcript \$\textbackslash{}mathcal H\$. A transcript-measurable orthogonal basis expresses the conditional matrix as a known matrix plus the Gram matrix of an independent standard Gaussian block of size \$(n-q)\textbackslash{}times(n-q)\$. Thus\newline{}\$\$\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(W)\textbackslash{}mid\textbackslash{}mathcal H=\allowbreak{}c(\textbackslash{}mathcal H)+Z,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad Z\textbackslash{}sim\textbackslash{}chi\textasciicircum{}2\_\allowbreak{}\{(n-q)\textasciicircum{}2\},\allowbreak{}\$\$\newline{}where \$Z\$ is independent of the transcript. Remove the component in the previously queried subspace from a dependent query. If the algorithm stops early,\allowbreak{} extend the transcript to \$q\$ independent directions;\allowbreak{} its output remains measurable with respect to the extended transcript. This only provides additional information. For randomized algorithms,\allowbreak{} condition first on the independent private seed,\allowbreak{} apply the lemma,\allowbreak{} and then integrate. Adaptivity is preserved throughout.\newline{}\newline{}**Hard distribution at small tolerance.** Assume \$0<\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}le1/\allowbreak{}384\$. For \$d\textbackslash{}ge4\$,\allowbreak{} set \$n=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}lfloor1/\allowbreak{}(96\textbackslash{}varepsilon)\textbackslash{}rfloor\textbackslash{}\}\$,\allowbreak{} so \$n\textbackslash{}ge4\$,\allowbreak{} and let \$A=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}operatorname\{diag\}(W,\allowbreak{}0\_\allowbreak{}\{d-n\})\$. A query in dimension \$d\$ returns the \$W\$ product of its first \$n\$ coordinates and a zero tail,\allowbreak{} exactly simulating one query in dimension \$n\$. The matrix \$A\$ is positive semidefinite and \$\textbackslash{}mathbb E\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)=\allowbreak{}n\textasciicircum{}2\$.\newline{}\newline{}**Anti-concentration.** Suppose \$q\textbackslash{}le n/\allowbreak{}2\$. For \$Z\textbackslash{}sim\textbackslash{}chi\textasciicircum{}2\_\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu\$ with \$\textbackslash{}nu\textbackslash{}ge4\$,\allowbreak{} the density is bounded by \$1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sqrt\textbackslash{}nu\$. Its maximum occurs at \$\textbackslash{}nu-2\$;\allowbreak{} the standard Stirling lower bound for the Gamma function,\allowbreak{} with \$a=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}nu/\allowbreak{}2\textbackslash{}ge2\$,\allowbreak{} gives the bound \$e(1-1/\allowbreak{}a)\textasciicircum{}\{a-1\}/\allowbreak{}(2\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2\textbackslash{}pi a\})\textbackslash{}le1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}sqrt\{2a\}\$. Here \$\textbackslash{}nu=\allowbreak{}(n-q)\textasciicircum{}2\$,\allowbreak{} so the conditional trace density is at most \$2/\allowbreak{}n\$. Markov's inequality gives \$\textbackslash{}Pr(\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)>4n\textasciicircum{}2)\textbackslash{}le1/\allowbreak{}4\$. On success and \$\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)\textbackslash{}le4n\textasciicircum{}2\$,\allowbreak{} the true trace lies in an interval of length \$8\textbackslash{}varepsilon n\textasciicircum{}2\$ centered at the transcript-measurable estimate \$\textbackslash{}widehat\textbackslash{}tau\$. Integrating the conditional density yields\newline{}\$\$\textbackslash{}Pr(\textbackslash{}text\{success\})\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}frac14+(8\textbackslash{}varepsilon n\textasciicircum{}2)\textbackslash{}frac2n=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}frac14+16\textbackslash{}varepsilon n\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}frac5\{12\}<\textbackslash{}frac23.\$\$\newline{}This contradicts success probability at least \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$ on every fixed input,\allowbreak{} which would imply average success at least \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$ under this admissible input distribution. Consequently the budget exceeds \$n/\allowbreak{}2\$,\allowbreak{} and \$n\$ is a universal constant multiple of \$\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\}\$.\newline{}\newline{}**Small dimensions.** For \$d<4\$,\allowbreak{} the output distribution of a zero-query algorithm is independent of the matrix. The permitted relative-error intervals for \$I\_\allowbreak{}d\$ and \$2I\_\allowbreak{}d\$ are disjoint when \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}le1/\allowbreak{}384\$. Both success probabilities therefore cannot be at least \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$. One necessary query gives the required constant-factor lower bound.\newline{}\newline{}**Remaining nontrivial tolerances.** Let \$1/\allowbreak{}384<\textbackslash{}varepsilon<1\$ and take any \$d\textbackslash{}ge1\$. Choose \$a\_\allowbreak{}0>(1+\textbackslash{}varepsilon)/\allowbreak{}(1-\textbackslash{}varepsilon)\$. The acceptable output intervals for \$I\_\allowbreak{}d\$ and \$a\_\allowbreak{}0I\_\allowbreak{}d\$ are\newline{}\$\$[(1-\textbackslash{}varepsilon)d,\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}varepsilon)d],\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}qquad [(1-\textbackslash{}varepsilon)a\_\allowbreak{}0d,\allowbreak{}(1+\textbackslash{}varepsilon)a\_\allowbreak{}0d],\allowbreak{}\$\$\newline{}and are disjoint. A zero-query algorithm has the same output distribution on both inputs,\allowbreak{} so its two success probabilities sum to at most \$1\$ and cannot both be at least \$2/\allowbreak{}3\$. The fixed budget is therefore at least \$1\$. Since \$\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\}\textbackslash{}le384\$,\allowbreak{}\newline{}\$\$N\textbackslash{}ge1\textbackslash{}ge\textbackslash{}frac1\{384\}\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\}.\$\$\newline{}Combining the constants gives the uniform lower bound \$\textbackslash{}Omega(\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\})\$ for all \$0<\textbackslash{}varepsilon<1\$. The scales of these inputs are neither revealed nor bounded,\allowbreak{} as required by the stated trace-estimation models.\newline{}\newline{}**Transfers.** The bound applies to nonadaptive algorithms,\allowbreak{} a subclass of adaptive algorithms. Bounded integer-coordinate queries are likewise a subclass of arbitrary real queries. The lower bound also applies at success probability \$0.9\$,\allowbreak{} uniformly for \$b\_\allowbreak{}\{\textbackslash{}mathrm q\}\textbackslash{}ge0\$. Together with the admissible Rademacher NA-Hutch++ upper bound and reconstruction in \$d\$ standard-basis queries,\allowbreak{} this yields \$\textbackslash{}Theta(\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\})\$. This is an explicit consequence of the cited posterior lemma,\allowbreak{} rather than a trace-estimation theorem attributed directly to that source.\newline{}\newline{}**Zero-query endpoint.** If \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}ge1\$,\allowbreak{} positive semidefiniteness implies \$\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)\textbackslash{}ge0\$,\allowbreak{} and the constant output \$\textbackslash{}widehat\textbackslash{}tau=\allowbreak{}0\$ satisfies\newline{}\$\$|\textbackslash{}widehat\textbackslash{}tau-\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)|=\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A)\textbackslash{}le\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}operatorname\{tr\}(A).\$\$\newline{}for every input. It works at every allowed confidence level,\allowbreak{} dimension,\allowbreak{} and integer query alphabet. Nonnegativity of query cost makes the optimum exactly \$0\$. The nontrivial-tolerance rate \$\textbackslash{}Theta(\textbackslash{}min\textbackslash{}\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}\})\$ therefore does not extend to \$\textbackslash{}varepsilon\textbackslash{}ge1\$.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Use Proposition 3 of Amsel et al.,\allowbreak{} arXiv:\allowbreak{}2402.09379v3,\allowbreak{} archived SHA256 efb3338e536779388499ff92beee30a07154993989b2a743138f51d620d246c1,\allowbreak{} PDF p.11 and Appendix B.1,\allowbreak{} pp.22{\AtlasUnicodeText –}\allowbreak{}23;\allowbreak{} read character ranges [26800,\allowbreak{}31000) and [51800,\allowbreak{}59600). Only its adaptive Wishart posterior lemma is used. Let G have n-by-n independent standard normal entries and W=\allowbreak{}G\textasciicircum{}T G. Any deterministic normalization in the source can be removed by known scaling,\allowbreak{} preserving relative error and query count. Condition on the independent private seed. After q<n independent adaptive query directions,\allowbreak{} the conditional trace is c(H)+Z,\allowbreak{} where c(H) is transcript-measurable and Z is independent chi-square with (n-q)\textasciicircum{}2 degrees of freedom. Dependent query directions provide no new information and can be removed;\allowbreak{} an early-stopping transcript can be extended to q independent directions,\allowbreak{} only giving additional information.\newline{}For 0<epsilon<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}384 and d>=\allowbreak{}4,\allowbreak{} set n=\allowbreak{}min\{d,\allowbreak{}floor(1/\allowbreak{}(96 epsilon))\}>=\allowbreak{}4 and A=\allowbreak{}diag(W,\allowbreak{}0). Each dimension-d query simulates one W query by taking its first n coordinates. Suppose the fixed budget q<=\allowbreak{}n/\allowbreak{}2. The density of chi-square\_\allowbreak{}nu for nu>=\allowbreak{}4 is at most 1/\allowbreak{}sqrt(nu):\allowbreak{} writing a=\allowbreak{}nu/\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} its maximum is (a-1)\textasciicircum{}(a-1) exp(-(a-1))/\allowbreak{}(2 Gamma(a));\allowbreak{} the Stirling lower bound gives at most e/\allowbreak{}(2 sqrt(2 pi a))<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}sqrt(2a). Thus the conditional trace density is at most 2/\allowbreak{}n. Since E trace(A)=\allowbreak{}n\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} Markov gives Pr(trace(A)>4n\textasciicircum{}2)<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4. On success with trace(A)<=\allowbreak{}4n\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} the true trace lies within 4 epsilon n\textasciicircum{}2 of the transcript-measurable output. Integrating the conditional density over that interval gives Pr(success)<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4+8 epsilon n\textasciicircum{}2(2/\allowbreak{}n)<=\allowbreak{}5/\allowbreak{}12. Integrating over the private seed preserves this bound. A per-input guarantee of 1-delta>1/\allowbreak{}2 would imply average success greater than 1/\allowbreak{}2 under this PSD input distribution,\allowbreak{} a contradiction. Hence q>n/\allowbreak{}2. Since floor(1/\allowbreak{}(96 epsilon))>=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}(192 epsilon),\allowbreak{} this implies q>=\allowbreak{}(1/\allowbreak{}384) min\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon\}.\newline{}For any d>=\allowbreak{}1 and epsilon<1,\allowbreak{} a zero-query algorithm has the same output distribution on A=\allowbreak{}0 and A=\allowbreak{}I\_\allowbreak{}d. Their successful output sets are \{0\} and [(1-epsilon)d,\allowbreak{}(1+epsilon)d],\allowbreak{} which are disjoint. Their success probabilities sum to at most one,\allowbreak{} contradicting both being at least 1-delta>1/\allowbreak{}2. Thus N>=\allowbreak{}1. If d<4,\allowbreak{} this gives N>=\allowbreak{}(1/\allowbreak{}384) min\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon\};\allowbreak{} if epsilon>1/\allowbreak{}384,\allowbreak{} it gives the same bound because min\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon\}<384. Combining cases proves the claimed uniform lower bound. This establishes no growing dependence on log(1/\allowbreak{}delta). For epsilon>=\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} the existing zero-output proof instead gives exact optimum zero.\par\endgroup

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Conditional premises:\allowbreak{} frozen /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}12,\allowbreak{} canonical hash 99191570a108dc5104236c31ea376e5016d1bbf81d98dea6f3c6129567dc949a,\allowbreak{} and /\allowbreak{}proofs/\allowbreak{}3,\allowbreak{} canonical hash d53440c5ae92d8938e60070893c939b7ab8ba8064c980ab1b2c25f44a49f9819,\allowbreak{} assert N\_\allowbreak{}ad>=\allowbreak{}min\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon\}/\allowbreak{}384 uniformly on the stated domain. These accepted premises are retained conditionally,\allowbreak{} not independently recertified. The complete native views,\allowbreak{} common specification,\allowbreak{} quantities and resource projections establish identical inputs,\allowbreak{} exact Av feedback,\allowbreak{} scalar relative-trace output,\allowbreak{} per-fixed-input probability and fixed worst-case single-vector query cost;\allowbreak{} only adaptivity differs.\newline{}Given any nonadaptive algorithm,\allowbreak{} an adaptive simulator samples the identical private seed,\allowbreak{} generates the same public-parameter-dependent query list,\allowbreak{} executes it in order without altering vectors from responses,\allowbreak{} and applies identical final postprocessing. Every fixed input and seed produces the same transcript,\allowbreak{} output and charged number of vector products. Blocks remain charged by columns. Thus N*\_\allowbreak{}nonadaptive>=\allowbreak{}N*\_\allowbreak{}adaptive pointwise in (d,\allowbreak{}epsilon,\allowbreak{}delta),\allowbreak{} proving the new nonadaptive lower with the unchanged constant 1/\allowbreak{}384. This is a directional comparison of distinct native quantities,\allowbreak{} not an identity merge. No external theorem,\allowbreak{} probability amplification or parameter substitution is introduced.\newline{}For the envelope retain native nonadaptive /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}5 and /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}7:\allowbreak{} upper O(min\{d,\allowbreak{}U\}),\allowbreak{} where L=\allowbreak{}log(1/\allowbreak{}delta),\allowbreak{} U=\allowbreak{}sqrt(L)/\allowbreak{}epsilon+L and m=\allowbreak{}min\{d,\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon\}. Retain /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}9 only on its exact native G=\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}regimes/\allowbreak{}6:\allowbreak{} delta<=\allowbreak{}exp(-4),\allowbreak{} epsilon<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}4 and d>=\allowbreak{}C*U. On G,\allowbreak{} F=\allowbreak{}sqrt(L)/\allowbreak{}epsilon if epsilon<=\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}0/\allowbreak{}sqrt(L),\allowbreak{} and F=\allowbreak{}L/\allowbreak{}log(L) otherwise. The combined lower is Omega(max\{m,\allowbreak{}F when G\}),\allowbreak{} omitting F outside G. Since L>=\allowbreak{}4 on G,\allowbreak{} its first branch has F>=\allowbreak{}2m. In its second branch 1/\allowbreak{}epsilon<sqrt(L)/\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}0 and log(L)<=\allowbreak{}sqrt(L),\allowbreak{} so F>=\allowbreak{}sqrt(L)>c\_\allowbreak{}0*m. Hence the guarded lower is equivalently Omega(F) on G and Omega(m) elsewhere,\allowbreak{} with universal constants. The old /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}8 slice lower has the same m rate. On the /\allowbreak{}bounds/\allowbreak{}6 source window,\allowbreak{} its accepted inequality N*>=\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}H/\allowbreak{}epsilon and reconstruction N*<=\allowbreak{}d imply d>=\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}H/\allowbreak{}epsilon,\allowbreak{} whence m>=\allowbreak{}min\{1,\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}H\}/\allowbreak{}epsilon. Thus that older lower is also redundant in asymptotic rate;\allowbreak{} exact constant dominance is not claimed.\newline{}For d<=\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}epsilon the upper d and lower d/\allowbreak{}384 give Theta(d),\allowbreak{} uniformly in delta. At d=\allowbreak{}1 the positive lower and integer budget force one query,\allowbreak{} attained by reconstruction. On G's first branch,\allowbreak{} L<=\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}0*sqrt(L)/\allowbreak{}epsilon implies U<=\allowbreak{}(1+c\_\allowbreak{}0)F,\allowbreak{} so the gap is constant. In the second branch U<=\allowbreak{}(1+1/\allowbreak{}c\_\allowbreak{}0)L,\allowbreak{} giving O(log L) gap. Outside G the ratio is O(min\{d,\allowbreak{}U\}/\allowbreak{}m),\allowbreak{} at most O(1+sqrt(L)+epsilon L). G is a sufficient source guard,\allowbreak{} not an intrinsic phase boundary;\allowbreak{} d\textasciitilde{}U is only an asymptotic crossover. epsilon=\allowbreak{}1 is excluded,\allowbreak{} and the retained endpoint comparisons give exact zero cost for epsilon>=\allowbreak{}1. Old populated comparisons are unchanged. Constant-success lower bounds also imply lower bounds for stronger success requirements,\allowbreak{} so newly registered coverage is not a claim of a novel rate for every newly displayed parameter tuple.\par\endgroup
